title: FACT SHEET: FCC Updates Covered List to Include Foreign-Produced Advanced Robotic Devices and Power Inverters

title: FCC Public Notice DA 26-786: Covered List update for foreign-produced power inverters and advanced robotic devices
key_claim: The Covered List entry for advanced robotic devices excepts only devices granted a Conditional Approval by the Department of War, which alone evaluates advanced robotic device submissions.
frame_summary: Sets the legal gate: a foreign-produced advanced robotic device is barred from FCC authorisation unless the Department of War clears it through a case-by-case Conditional Approval.

title: World Robotics 2026: EU-27 installations (press release)
key_claim: EU-27 installations fell to 60,500 units in 2025, an 11% contraction; automotive installed 14,900 units, down 25%; Germany's 24,800 units are 41% of the EU market; first Chinese suppliers have set up European distribution hubs and US-style trade restrictions might fuel the trend.
frame_summary: Describes a European market that is shrinking in the very year Chinese suppliers begin building European sales channels, and links their entry to trade restrictions elsewhere.
verbatim_quote: Trade restrictions in other key markets like the United States might further fuel this trend.
verbatim_list: The automotive industry installed 14,900 units in 2025
24,800 industrial robot installations account for 41% of the total EU market.
first Chinese suppliers have already established European distribution hubs.

title: World Robotics 2026: China installations (press release)
key_claim: China deployed 354,000 industrial robots in 2025, Chinese suppliers reached 55% of installations, foreign robots grew 27%, and the IFR expects 5% to 10% average annual growth to 2029.
frame_summary: Shows China as the volume centre of the robot market, with domestic suppliers holding a majority at home while foreign suppliers still grow.
verbatim_quote: A total of 354,000 units were deployed in 2025.
verbatim_list: Installations of foreign robots were up 27% in 2025.

title: New Restrictions Seek to Exclude Chinese Robotics from U.S. Market
key_claim: The ban excludes non-mobile robots, does not distinguish by intended use, and first exemptions have gone to Husqvarna and ANSCER platforms; a pending Section 232 investigation could bring tariffs, quotas, license fees or other import restrictions.
frame_summary: Reads the FCC listing together with tariffs and the Section 232 probe as a layered effort to keep Chinese robotics out of the US market, while noting the carve-outs and the exemption route.
verbatim_quote: The ban does not differentiate on the basis of intended use – whether consumer, industrial, or military.

title: China installs 59% of new factory robots as EU installations fall 11%
key_claim: Chinese brands sold 195,000 robots, 55% of their home market and down from 57% in 2024 as foreign suppliers grew 27%; the IFR forecasts no European growth in 2026 and 6% a year from 2027 to 2029.
frame_summary: Reports the IFR data as a China-and-America story in which Europe lags, and notes that Chinese domestic suppliers lost a little home share even as they sold more.
verbatim_quote: That gave them 55% of their home market, down from 57% in 2024, as foreign suppliers grew faster, by 27%.
verbatim_list: China installs 59% of new factory robots as EU installations fall 11%
Chinese brands sold 195,000 of those robots, up 15%.
It forecasts 11% growth in Asia this year, 2% in the Americas and none in Europe.
From 2027 to 2029, it expects Europe to grow by 6% a year, ahead of the Americas at 2% but behind Asia at 8%.

title: US robotics restrictions could drive more Chinese suppliers toward Europe, warns Exotec
key_claim: Exotec's chief revenue officer says the US measures could make Europe more attractive to some non-US suppliers, especially Chinese manufacturers, but it is too early to say competition will rise significantly, and Europe has no blanket ban on foreign warehouse robots.
frame_summary: Gives a warehouse-robot vendor's view that the US rules shift the competitive risk toward Europe, tempered by caution that the effect is unproven and that origin alone is no protection.
verbatim_quote: However, it is too early to say that they will lead to a significant increase in Chinese competition in Europe.
verbatim_list: Europe has not introduced a blanket ban on foreign-made warehouse robots.
European companies should not assume that their origin alone provides an exemption.
notes: Trade-press report of a vendor executive's views; vendor interest in the policy outcome, so used directionally. Fetched live via WebFetch 17/10/2026; device audit egress blocked, quote span(s) confirmed by hand against the live page text returned by WebFetch.
